note: Linux CI measurements. allocations is the tight signal; wall_s is a coarse backstop. Refresh by triggering release-gate.yml, downloading the bench-baseline-* artifact, and committing its targets here. Recalibrated at the v0.4.0 cut (#1046): allocations ROSE 80.5% (23,670,693 -> 42,721,526), wall_s 72.7% (25.579 -> 44.179) and peak_rss_kb 16.5% (483,252 -> 563,060), accepted as the cost of the cycle by maintainer ruling on 2026-09-27. The rise is two effects compounded, measured locally on macOS by running each engine over each tree in a fresh process (the local v0.3.9-on-v0.3.9 arm reproduced the CI baseline to 0.2%, and master-on-master reproduced this run to 0.1%): the benchmarked corpus is Rigor's own lib, which grew 26% in lines (108,297 -> 136,672), so the v0.3.9 engine alone allocates 34.75M over the new lib (+46.8% against this baseline); and the engine itself costs +19.1% allocations and +36% wall over the frozen v0.3.9 lib (23.71M -> 28.24M, 14.0s -> 19.1s), and +22.9% allocations over the grown lib (34.75M -> 42.72M). #1046 had accepted +6.8% on 2026-09-17, but that figure ran each merge over its own growing lib and was taken after #1045; on the frozen v0.3.9 lib the same stretch is +2.66%. The rest of the engine share was not attributed per merge before the cut. The per-merge sweep over the frozen corpus that followed is docs/notes/20260927-v040-engine-allocation-attribution.md (#1469). Sampling rule (#987): each gate run takes 2 reps per target, EACH IN A FRESH PROCESS (VmHWM is a per-process high-water mark, so an in-process rep can never report lower RSS, and a warm rep's wall is not comparable with this cold baseline), and records the LOWER of the reps for wall_s and peak_rss_kb while allocations and diagnostics are taken from the first rep unreduced. Measure a recalibration the same way -- bench/baseline.updated.json is already reduced, so committing its targets preserves the rule.
